text: state is a pure function of the event log; state.json is only a cache

section: spawn — bring an agent up, and prove what its provider can prove
text: a spawn that cannot be proven kills its own window and cleans up
payload is written to the inbox first; the keystroke is a doorbell, never the message
three gates — busy/dead, copy-mode, dirty composer — leave the message queued
from-seq defaults to the live end, so history cannot cause a false match
the outbox is the machine channel; replies are never parsed from the screen
an agent whose window vanished is recorded dead exactly once, however often you look
graceful /exit is best-effort; the timeout is the real guarantee
awaiting_human means stop; the orchestrator does not answer on the human’s behalf
workers learn identity from the environment, never by typing it

section: Check your inbox at the start of every turn
text: the worker re-reads its inbox at the start of every turn, lowest number first
a worker never passes --run or --agent to reply
the bootstrap’s Initial assignment is the first task; role and protocol are not assignments
a worker never assumes the orchestrator can see its screen
a worker never spawns, closes, or reaps another worker
